narrative.overview:
A lab notebook is kept by the person using it. It holds what was run and what was checked, in order, and the next entry starts where the last one stopped. Each site in this family is such a notebook: opening it puts the owner back at the place they stopped, with the next thing to do in view. The record line in the page gutter and its "stopped here" mark are what a reader should remember.

The material is cool paper, blue-black ink, thin ruling and one review red, with a blue-black night twin. Pages are dense and quiet. Structure comes from hairlines and a shared left edge, not boxes, and nothing is there for decoration. The family rejects the template it shipped before: giant headline, tilted terminal, two buttons, stats row, card grid.

The family shares a language, not a layout. Each site's structure follows its own content, so copy these rules and never a sibling's page. `kit/v1/notebook.css` is the source of truth for values, and this file explains how to use them. It was recorded from two built surfaces: the project index in this repository and the C# design patterns course (course index, lesson, guide, quiz, playground).
keyCharacteristics: A record line in the gutter: solid for what is done, dashed for what is not, with one red tick where the owner stopped.
Red only for "stopped here" and verified marks.
Pasted output between hairlines, with no window chrome.
Commands on their own line, never broken inside a token.
Noto Serif SC 600 for page heads, a Chinese-tuned sans for reading, Cascadia Mono for code.
Chinese page titles that break between phrases, never inside a word.
Flat, flush-left, square-cornered, and the way back to the stopped place first.

rules.name: The Review Red Rule
rules.body: Red means "stopped here" or "verified", and nothing else. Errors, warnings, links, hover states, emphasis and section accents never use it. Audit test: a page with no record and nothing verified has no red on it.

rules.name: The Line Not Hue Rule
rules.body: State is shown by line form and a written word, never by a new hue. The palette has no green, amber or blue status color. A correct quiz answer gets a 2px solid ink rule and 正确, a wrong one gets a dashed rule and 你的选择, and a locked step gets a dashed box. Audit test: in grayscale the page still says what is done.

rules.name: The Achromatic Field Rule
rules.body: Text fields carry no color of their own: transparent fill, Strong Ruling outline, Soft Ink placeholder and the ink focus ring.

rules.name: The One Serif Weight Rule
rules.body: The shared font files hold Noto Serif SC at weight 600 only, so the serif appears at 600 and never for reading text. `theme.js` adds `/kit/v1/fonts.css` on the production host only, so a local preview showing a fallback serif is expected.

rules.name: The Whole Phrase Rule
rules.body: Page titles use `word-break: keep-all` with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. In Chinese this limits breaks to spaces and punctuation, so 设计模式 stays whole, and `anywhere` remains as the emergency exit that stops a long title overflowing a phone. The kit sets this on every first-level heading. Add the same pair to anything else that shows a course or lesson title in the serif, such as the continue link. Write titles with natural break points (a space, `：`, `·`), because a long run with none gets cut wherever the emergency break lands.

rules.name: The No Balance Rule
rules.body: Don't use `text-wrap: balance` on Chinese text. It was tried on headings and removed because it split 下单 in the middle of a word on the OnlineStore guide title: it looks for equal line lengths, and Chinese offers it a break between any two characters, with no word boundaries to respect. `text-wrap: pretty` stays on headings and paragraphs for last-line orphans, but it does not stop mid-word splits either, which is why the Whole Phrase Rule exists.

rules.name: The Chinese Reading Rule
rules.body: Every page sets `lang="zh-CN"` and lets the kit's body settings reach the text: `line-break: strict` for line-start and line-end punctuation, `text-spacing-trim: trim-start` so an opening `（` at the start of a line does not look indented, `text-autospace: normal` for spacing between Chinese and Latin, and line height 1.75. An engine's stylesheet must not override them.

rules.name: The Wide Marks Rule
rules.body: Quotation marks, em dashes and ellipses come from a CJK face, because Latin UI faces draw them too narrow for Chinese. The kit does this with the `NB CJK Marks` face at the front of the sans stack, using `unicode-range`. Keep that face first if an engine's font variable is replaced.

rules.name: The Literal Code Rule
rules.body: Code uses Cascadia Mono, not Cascadia Code, with ligatures off, so `--` and `->` read exactly as they are typed. Put it first in the stack, because a `font:` shorthand resets the kit's ligature setting.

rules.name: The Flush Left Rule
rules.body: All text is left-aligned on one left edge, and nothing is centered: no centered headings, copy blocks or empty states. Only secondary things sit at the far edge: the head nav, the search box, the state column, the next link. The one centered thing is the capped page block in a window wider than 72rem.

rules.name: The Continue First Rule
rules.body: The way back to the stopped place is the first action on a site's opening screen, and nothing above it pitches the site. On the index it is a row at the top left, under 200px from the top of the window. On a course it sits directly under the title, beside the thing to run. With no record yet, it offers the first step or says plainly that there is no record.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. If something needs separating, rule a line.

rules.name: The Square Box Rule
rules.body: Anything drawn as a box has 2px corners or none: controls, dialogs and the favicon tile at 2px, pasted output, toasts and rows at none. Nothing is a pill. Radio buttons stay native and round.

rules.name: The Solid And Dashed Rule
rules.body: In the record line, solid means done and dashed means not done, so gaps in the work read as breaks in the line. Solid is never drawn for progress that is not on record, and dashed is never used as decoration.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: Lists and grouped content are rows between hairlines. No row or panel gets a fill, a radius or a shadow.

rules.name: The No Window Chrome Rule
rules.body: Output has hairlines above and below on the Pasted Sheet, and that is all: no title bar, traffic lights, tab strip, tilt, shadow or dark window on a light page.

rules.name: The Whole Token Rule
rules.body: A command never wraps and never breaks inside a token. It sits on its own line in the sheet with `white-space: pre`, `overflow-x: auto` and `min-width: 0`, and a long one scrolls sideways in its own box, even if that cuts it off at the edge of a phone. Anything meant to be copied gets a command row, and inline code is for short names.

dos: **Do** take every color from the kit's tokens and let `data-theme` switch them.
**Do** give every list of work a record line: solid for what is done, dashed for what is not, with one red tick at the stopped place.
**Do** check a page with no record on it. It should show no red.
**Do** build lists as ruled rows, with each site choosing its own columns from its own content.
**Do** paste real output on the sheet between 1px hairlines.
**Do** give each command its own line with `white-space: pre` and `overflow-x: auto`.
**Do** keep `word-break: keep-all` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on page titles, and write those titles with natural break points.
**Do** set `lang="zh-CN"` and keep `line-break: strict`, `text-spacing-trim: trim-start` and `text-autospace: normal` reaching the text.
**Do** show state with line form and a written word.
**Do** put the continue link first on a site's opening screen.
**Do** carry over the kit's reduced-motion and forced-colors handling when an engine replaces a component.
**Do** show only counts that come from the repository or the owner's own record.
donts: **Don't** use red for errors, warnings, links, hover states, emphasis or accents.
**Don't** add status colors. There is no green, amber or blue state in this palette.
**Don't** draw a dashed line as decoration, or a solid record line for work that is not on record.
**Don't** use cards: no filled tiles, rounded panels or grids of boxes.
**Don't** draw a terminal: no title bar, traffic lights, tab strip, tilt or shadow around output.
**Don't** remove `keep-all` from a page title because it breaks badly; shorten the title or give it a break point.
**Don't** center headings, copy or empty states.
**Don't** open a site with the old template: giant headline, tilted terminal, two buttons, stats row, card grid.
**Don't** use shadows, blur or pill shapes.
**Don't** set reading text in the serif, or use the serif at any weight but 600.
**Don't** use uppercase, letter-spacing or justified text.
**Don't** add icons. Controls are words, and the only drawn marks are the record line, the tick and the check.
**Don't** put a small label above a title. Keys and categories get their own column or row.
**Don't** edit a site's copy of the kit, or change a published kit version.
**Don't** copy a sibling site's page structure. The family shares rules, not a template.
